purpose: Create and run a new container from an image. Pulls the image if missing (controlled by --pull). Aliases: `docker run`. The most commonly invoked Docker subcommand; surface area is enormous (~115 flags). Failure paths: image not found, port conflict, mount source missing, OOM-kill, exit-code 125 (daemon error before runtime), 126 (entrypoint not executable), 127 (not found).

flags.name: -d, --detach
flags.doc: Run container in background and print container ID.

flags.name: --name
flags.doc: Assign a name to the container; used as DNS name on user-defined networks.

flags.name: --rm
flags.doc: Automatically remove the container and its anonymous volumes when it exits.

flags.name: -i, --interactive
flags.doc: Keep STDIN open even if not attached.

flags.name: -t, --tty
flags.doc: Allocate a pseudo-TTY (often combined with -i for an interactive shell).

flags.name: -p, --publish
flags.doc: Publish a container's port(s) to the host. Multiple times allowed. Without --publish-all, ports are not externally reachable.

flags.name: -P, --publish-all
flags.doc: Publish all EXPOSE'd ports to random ephemeral host ports.

flags.name: -e, --env
flags.doc: Set an environment variable. Multiple times allowed.

flags.name: --env-file
flags.doc: Read env vars from a file (one KEY=VAL per line).

flags.name: -v, --volume
flags.doc: Bind-mount a host path or volume into the container. Short form.

flags.name: --mount
flags.doc: Attach a filesystem mount. Verbose, explicit alternative to -v; required for volume-driver options.

flags.name: --tmpfs
flags.doc: Mount a tmpfs into the container at the given path.

flags.name: --volume-driver
flags.doc: Optional volume driver for the container.

flags.name: --stop-signal
flags.doc: Signal sent on `docker stop` (default SIGTERM, or image's STOPSIGNAL).

flags.name: --stop-timeout
flags.doc: Grace period before SIGKILL on `docker stop`. -1 for unbounded.

flags.name: --init
flags.doc: Run docker-init/tini as pid 1 to forward signals and reap zombies.

flags.name: --health-cmd
flags.doc: Command run periodically to test container health.

flags.name: --health-retries
flags.doc: Consecutive failures before container is marked unhealthy.

flags.name: --health-timeout
flags.doc: Max time for one health-check command to run.

flags.name: --health-start-period
flags.doc: Initial wait before health-retries countdown begins.

flags.name: --health-start-interval
flags.doc: Health-check cadence during the start period.

flags.name: --no-healthcheck
flags.doc: Disable any HEALTHCHECK baked into the image.

flags.name: --memory, -m
flags.doc: Hard memory limit. Hitting it triggers OOM-killer (exit 137).

flags.name: --memory-reservation
flags.doc: Soft memory limit (kernel attempts to keep usage below).

flags.name: --memory-swappiness
flags.doc: Tune kernel swappiness for the container.

flags.name: --oom-kill-disable
flags.doc: Disable OOM-killer (use with care; can wedge the host).

flags.name: --oom-score-adj
flags.doc: Tune host OOM preference for the container.

flags.name: --cpus
flags.doc: Number of CPUs (computed in CFS quota/period).

flags.name: --pids-limit
flags.doc: Tune container pids cgroup limit. -1 = unlimited.

flags.name: --device
flags.doc: Pass a host device through to the container.

flags.name: --device-cgroup-rule
flags.doc: Add a rule to the cgroup devices allowlist.

flags.name: --cap-add
flags.doc: Add a Linux capability (e.g. NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE).

flags.name: --cap-drop
flags.doc: Drop a Linux capability; combine with selective --cap-add for least-privilege.

flags.name: --privileged
flags.doc: All capabilities + host device access; disables AppArmor/seccomp. Equivalent to root on host (avoid).

flags.name: --security-opt
flags.doc: Security option: seccomp=<file>, apparmor=<profile>, label=…, no-new-privileges:true.

flags.name: --read-only
flags.doc: Mount root filesystem read-only (writes to /tmp etc require explicit --tmpfs).

flags.name: --user, -u
flags.doc: User/uid to run as inside the container.

flags.name: --entrypoint
flags.doc: Override image ENTRYPOINT. `--entrypoint=sh` is the canonical 'shell-out into a broken container' move.

flags.name: --label, -l
flags.doc: Set metadata label on the container.

flags.name: --label-file
flags.doc: Read labels from a file (one per line).

flags.name: --network
flags.doc: Connect to a network. `host` uses the host's network namespace (no isolation).

flags.name: --ip
flags.doc: Static IPv4 (only on user-defined networks with --subnet).

flags.name: --add-host
flags.doc: Add an entry to /etc/hosts. `host-gateway` resolves to the host (Linux).

flags.name: --pid
flags.doc: PID namespace mode. `host` shares the host's pid ns (debugging only).

flags.name: --userns
flags.doc: Disable user-namespace remap for this container (`host` is the only valid value).

flags.name: --gpus
flags.doc: GPU devices to add (requires NVIDIA Container Toolkit).

flags.name: --runtime
flags.doc: OCI runtime to use (runc, crun, io.containerd.kata.v2, etc.).

flags.name: --platform
flags.doc: Force platform when image is multi-arch (e.g. `linux/amd64`).

flags.name: --pull
flags.doc: When to pull the image. Default `missing`.

flags.name: --storage-opt
flags.doc: Per-container storage driver option (e.g. size on devicemapper).

flags.name: --sysctl
flags.doc: Set a sysctl in the container's namespaces.

flags.name: --cidfile
flags.doc: Write the container ID to this file (PID-file pattern).

flags.name: --detach-keys
flags.doc: Override the key sequence for detaching from an attached container.

purpose: List containers. Aliases: `docker ps`, `docker container list`, `docker container ps`. By default shows running only. Filter expressions are the meat — `--filter status=exited`, `--filter health=unhealthy`, `--filter exited=137` are interview-day staples.

flags.name: -f, --filter
flags.doc: Filter output. Keys: id, name, label, exited, status, ancestor, before, since, volume, network, publish, expose, health, isolation, is-task.

flags.name: --format
flags.doc: Custom output format. `--format json` for machine consumption.

flags.name: -q, --quiet
flags.doc: Only display container IDs (good for piping into `xargs docker rm`).

flags.name: -s, --size
flags.doc: Display total file sizes (writable layer + virtual).

purpose: Execute a command in a RUNNING container. Aliases: `docker exec`. Fails on paused/stopped containers. The command isn't restarted with the container; chained commands need explicit `sh -c`.

flags.name: -e, --env
flags.doc: Set env vars for the exec process (overrides container env).

flags.name: --privileged
flags.doc: Extended privileges for the exec command (separate from --privileged on run).

purpose: Fetch logs from a container. Aliases: `docker logs`. Works only with `json-file`, `local`, and `journald` log drivers; with `fluentd`/`syslog`/etc., the daemon doesn't keep a local cache and `docker logs` returns nothing.

flags.name: --details
flags.doc: Show extra details (env, labels) provided to --log-opt.

flags.name: --since
flags.doc: Show logs since RFC3339 / Unix timestamp / Go duration (e.g. 42m).

flags.name: -n, --tail
flags.doc: Lines from the end of the log (default: all).

flags.name: --until
flags.doc: Show logs before timestamp (paired with --since for slicing).

examples.expected_output: last 100 log lines + new ones streaming
errors in the last 10 minutes

examples.scenario: slice for a known incident time

purpose: Send SIGTERM (or configured stop-signal), wait for grace period, then SIGKILL. Aliases: `docker stop`. Exit semantics: clean if app handles signal; otherwise 137 (128+9). The 10-second-then-SIGKILL pattern is responsible for many 'docker stop hangs' tickets.

flags.name: -s, --signal
flags.doc: Override stop signal (e.g. SIGINT). Image's STOPSIGNAL or `--stop-signal` is used otherwise.

flags.name: -t, --timeout
flags.doc: Grace period before SIGKILL. Default 10s (Linux) / 30s (Windows). -1 = unlimited.

examples.expected_output: container exits cleanly within grace period
30s grace before SIGKILL
sends SIGINT instead of SIGTERM
examples.scenario: app responds to Ctrl-C semantics rather than SIGTERM

purpose: Send a signal (default SIGKILL) to the container's pid 1. Aliases: `docker kill`. With shell-form ENTRYPOINT/CMD, signals go to /bin/sh -c not the real binary — root cause of 'docker kill -s SIGUSR1 doesn't reach my app'. Fix: exec-form or `--init`.

flags.name: -s, --signal
flags.doc: Signal to send (name, e.g. SIGHUP, or number, e.g. 1). Default SIGKILL.

examples.expected_output: container terminated immediately (SIGKILL)

purpose: Display detailed JSON for one or more containers (config, state, mounts, networks, log config, restart-policy). The single most useful debugging command: every field of `docker inspect` is queryable via `--format`.

flags.name: -f, --format
flags.doc: Format output. `--format '{{.State.Health.Status}}'` extracts health status; `--format json` for full JSON.

flags.name: -s, --size
flags.doc: Include total file sizes (writable layer + virtual).

examples.scenario: check exit code of last run (137 = OOM, 139 = SEGV, 143 = SIGTERM)

purpose: Start one or more stopped containers. Aliases: `docker start`. Reuses the previous run-config (env, mounts, port publish) — no re-spec. Useful after `docker stop` and after host reboot if `--restart` policy isn't set.

flags.doc: Attach STDOUT/STDERR to the started container.

purpose: Remove one or more containers. Aliases: `docker rm`. Fails on running containers unless `-f`. Removing frees the writable layer; named volumes attached are NOT removed (use `-v` for anonymous volumes).

flags.name: -f, --force
flags.doc: Force-remove a running container (sends SIGKILL first).

flags.name: -v, --volumes
flags.doc: Also remove any anonymous volumes attached to the container.

purpose: The Docker daemon process itself. Self-sufficient runtime for containers; reads /etc/docker/daemon.json by default. Most flags map 1:1 to daemon.json keys (catalogued in docker.engine.cfg.daemon.json). Failure-modes: 'unable to configure the Docker daemon with file /etc/docker/daemon.json: invalid character …' on bad JSON; 'the following directives are specified both as a flag and in the configuration file' on dual-spec.

flags.name: -H, --host
flags.doc: Daemon socket(s) to listen on. Multiple times allowed.

flags.name: --containerd
flags.doc: containerd socket address (when using external containerd).

flags.name: --live-restore
flags.doc: Keep containers running across daemon restart/upgrade.

flags.name: --no-new-privileges
flags.doc: Set no-new-privileges by default for new containers.

flags.name: --default-cgroupns-mode
flags.doc: Default cgroup-ns mode for new containers.

flags.name: --init
flags.doc: Inject docker-init as pid 1 by default.

flags.name: --icc
flags.doc: Inter-container communication on default bridge (default true).

flags.name: --ip-masq
flags.doc: IP masquerading on default bridge (default true).

flags.name: --default-address-pool
flags.doc: Default address pool for user-defined networks.

flags.name: --userland-proxy
flags.doc: Use userland-proxy for loopback traffic (default true).

flags.name: --insecure-registry
flags.doc: Allow insecure (HTTP / self-signed) communication with this registry.

flags.name: --rootless
flags.doc: Enable rootless mode (typically used via RootlessKit).

flags.name: --http-proxy
flags.doc: HTTP proxy URL for daemon outgoing traffic.

flags.name: --tlsverify
flags.doc: Use TLS and verify the remote (mTLS).

flags.name: --tlscacert
flags.doc: Trust certs signed only by this CA.

flags.name: --label
flags.doc: Set daemon-level labels (surfaced in docker info).

flags.name: --validate
flags.doc: Validate daemon configuration and exit (no daemon start).

flags.name: --allow-direct-routing
flags.doc: Allow remote access to published ports on container IP addresses.
